title: OpenClaw in Your Hand: Building a Physical AI Terminal - Lech Kalinowski, Callstack
talk_summary: A hardware hobbyist talk about building a handheld ESP32 terminal with dual OLED/e-paper displays that acts as a remote control for an OpenClaw agent backed by a local 120B model served via TensorRT with an OpenAI-style proxy. Almost all content is embedded firmware, power management, and an RPG game demo, with no agent-orchestration or review methodology.

takeaways.technique: OpenAI-compatible proxy in front of self-hosted model
takeaways.what_they_do: They serve a local 120B model with TensorRT and expose it through an OpenAI-style proxy because many open-source models don't match the OpenAI API shape.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I just exposed OpenAI style to uh also like LLM proxy because I just hit a lot of walls with uh other open source models

takeaways.technique: Pre-allocated fixed buffers, no dynamic allocation on constrained node
takeaways.what_they_do: Pages live in pre-allocated memory with no markdown engine and no malloc on the MCU, giving fast, predictable rendering.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the pages live in a pre-allocated memory. There's a no markdown engine and no malloc on the MCU side

takeaways.what_they_do: The device keeps working if any one component fails: e-paper if OLED dies, encoder if keyboard dies, local shell if Wi-Fi dies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the LED doesn't work, you the e-paper works. If the cardboard doesn't work... then you'll you have an encoder
